analysis.investment_thesis: Nazara is a serial gaming acquirer trading at 100.8x EV/EBITDA with a 1.98% operating margin and negative FCF — the price reflects a perfection scenario that the financials simply do not support. Second-level thinking demands we ask what the consensus is missing: this is a roll-up story funded by continuous equity dilution, not an organically compounding business.
key_strengths: Revenue 9Y CAGR of 25.5% (₹211 Cr → ₹1,624 Cr), showing strong top-line expansion via acquisitions
Minimal balance-sheet debt (D/E 0.06) with ₹299 Cr cash, so near-term solvency risk is low
High gross margin (71.4%) confirms software/digital IP economics if operational leverage can ever be achieved
key_risks: Valuation is extreme: 100.8x EV/EBITDA on 1.98% operating margins leaves zero margin of safety
Growth is entirely acquisition-driven — investing outflows of ₹1,139 Cr in FY25 alone, funded by ₹805 Cr financing inflows (serial dilution)
Net profit actually fell YoY (₹75 Cr → ₹51 Cr in FY25) despite 43% revenue growth — acquisitions are not accretive at the margin
red_flags: OCF yield of ~0.65% (₹66 Cr / ₹10,126 Cr market cap) vs. my 6-8% threshold — you are paying 150x operating cash flow
Equity base tripled in 3 years (₹1,041 Cr → ₹3,395 Cr) — minority shareholders are being systematically diluted to fund the roll-up
Net profit CAGR of -2.7% over 9 years despite 25.5% revenue CAGR — scale is not converting to earnings
'Other Income' of ₹80 Cr in FY25 nearly matches operating profit of ₹115 Cr — core operating economics are far weaker than headline numbers suggest
FCF turned negative (-₹82 Cr) in FY25 as capex surged to ₹148 Cr — the cash engine is running in reverse
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The cardinal sin in investing is paying a full price for optionality without a margin of safety. At 100.8x EV/EBITDA and a 1.98% operating margin, Nazara requires near-flawless execution for years simply to justify today's price — and any stumble means permanent capital loss, not a temporary setback. The business model is a roll-up: raise equity, buy gaming IPs or studios, report revenue growth, repeat. This flatters revenue CAGRs but destroys per-share value. Over nine years, revenues grew 25.5% annually while net profits compounded at -2.7%. That is not a growth story — that is an accounting story.

What troubles me most is the asymmetric risk/reward at this price. Even in an optimistic scenario where EBITDA doubles to ₹400 Cr by FY27, you are still paying 25x forward EV/EBITDA — generous for Indian gaming where no durable moat has been demonstrated. In a stress scenario — a funding winter, an acquisition that sours, or simply margin compression — the downside is 60-70% from here with no FCF floor to arrest the fall. ROCE of 2.5% confirms the company is destroying economic value with every rupee deployed. This is precisely the situation I most fear: a story stock at cycle-peak enthusiasm, where the consensus sees only upside and ignores the compounding dilution of minority shareholders.
